correctness.rationale: For every b>=0 and a in R the boundary conditions hold and an exact twice-differentiated numerator N is verified symbolically. Fixing t=(1-x)(1-y) makes N affine in (1-x)+(1-y), reducing positivity to diagonal and axis endpoints. For a=-k<=0 necessity is N(0,1)<0 when k>b+1; sufficiency for 0<=k<=b+1 uses P=k/(1+b exp(w))<=1, Pw<=1 (w=k t<=k), and h<=1-xy to prove N>=0 globally. Positive a has strictly positive axis numerator, so the explicit diagonal inequality is necessary and sufficient. For (2,1), an analytic exp inequality establishes all diagonal inequalities; for (21,20) a rational Taylor bracket for exp(7/3) proves a strictly negative interior density. These are infinite-domain proofs; the checker validates identities and exact witness, not a finite-grid substitute.

value.rationale: The originating OR3 paper restricts its usable parameters to |a|<=1. The complete sharp negative domain a>=-(b+1) supplies arbitrarily larger admissible positive-dependence strengths for fixed larger b, while the positive-side diagonal obstruction shows that merely imposing the symmetric corner bound is unsafe. The (2,1) admission and (21,20) counterexample establish operationally consequential domain asymmetry for model fitting. This is an object-motivated sharp boundary, not a computational enumeration or a trivial relabeling.
